This change addresses the following two issues:

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/1968
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/2012

This change redesigns the chat streaming model to avoid committing
partial rows into scrollback. While streaming, partial content is shown
only in a transient live overlay above the composer. When a stream
completes, the assistant answer and the reasoning are each rendered as
a single Markdown block in the conversation history, preceded by clear
section headers for readability. In addition, the live overlay behavior
and preview width are now configurable via CLI flags, and these options
are plumbed through the TUI to the ChatWidget.
    
Summary:

- Add CLI flags: --max-cols, --live-rows; plumb through App → ChatWidget.
- Implement live ring overlay with soft‑wrap by default; hard‑cap via --max-cols.
- Redesign streaming: avoid committing partial rows; use overlay during stream.
- Finalize: render assistant answer and reasoning as single markdown blocks.
- Emit section headers (thinking/codex) at finalize for tidy history.
- Default to no preview width cap; remove hard 80‑col pin.
- Respect preview width for tool previews when --max-cols is set.

### Context  
Fixes #2779 – when autocompleting file paths preceded by `@`, the prefix is currently dropped. For example, typing `@REA` and selecting `README.md` yields `README.md` instead of `@README.md`.  

### Root Cause  
The completion logic does not restore the leading `@` when applying the suggestion.  

### Solution  
Ensure the `@` prefix is preserved and prepended to the completed path.  

### Why This Matters  
Preserving the `@` allows developers to continue modifying autocompleted paths and still receive further suggestions, since the path remains valid with the `@` prefix. Moreover, prompts containing `@path` are correctly interpreted by the LLM, so retaining the prefix after completion is both accurate and useful.  

---  
Closes #2779.
items.title: Fix: Preserve '@' prefix in file path autocomplete #2779

## Summary

issue: #2961

Adds approval pending notifications that alert users when command execution or file modifications require approval, providing structured information about what is awaiting approval.

## What Changed

- Added new notification types for approval pending states:
  - PendingCommandApproval: Notifies when shell command execution requires approval
  - PendingFileApproval: Notifies when file modifications require approval
- Structured command information: Command notifications include the full command as an array of strings
- Structured file change information: File notifications include an array of FileChangeInfo objects with:
  - operation: Operation type ("A", "D", "M" for Add/Delete/Modify)
  - path: File path being modified
  - new_path: Destination path for rename operations (optional)
- Added FileChangeInfo struct to represent individual file operations

## Why This Change

Users can now be alerted when:

- Commands are waiting for execution approval
- File modifications are waiting for approval

## How It Works

Command approval notifications:
```
{
  "type": "pending-command-approval",
  "turn-id": "123",
  "command": ["rm", "-rf", "/tmp/test"]
}
```

File approval notifications:
```
{
  "type": "pending-file-approval",
  "turn-id": "12345",
  "changes": [
    { "operation": "A", "path": "/path/to/new_file.rs", "new-path": null },
    { "operation": "D", "path": "/path/to/deleted_file.rs", "new-path": null },
    { "operation": "M", "path": "/path/to/existing.rs", "new-path": null },
    { "operation": "M", "path": "/path/to/old_file.rs", "new-path": "/path/to/renamed_file.rs"}
  ]
}
```

## Testing

- All tests passing
- New tests added for both notification types
items.title: feat: Add approval pending notifications for command execution and file modifications

# What I Changed

1. Early auth guard in codex-core: Added CodexErr::NotAuthenticated with a clear message: "not authenticated: please log in (run codex login) or set an API key".
2. Auth preflight in stream(): In codex_core::client::ModelClient::stream, added a preflight check for providers that require authentication:
   - If a provider-specific API key env var is present, proceed
   - Else, if an AuthManager token exists, proceed
   - Else:
     - If the provider declared a required env var but it's missing, return that precise EnvVar error
     - Otherwise, return NotAuthenticated immediately (no HTTP attempts, no retries)
3. Non-retryable error handling: In codex_core::codex::run_turn, treated NotAuthenticated as non-retryable (same as EnvVar), so the agent does not sit in "Working" and repeatedly retry.

## Why This Fix Issue

Previously, when not logged in, requests would still be attempted, leading to a prolonged "Working" state. Now, if you press Ctrl+C on the login screen and try to send a message without being authenticated, Codex returns an error immediately, avoiding the infinite "Working" loop.

## Files Touched

- codex-rs/core/src/error.rs: Added NotAuthenticated error variant.
- codex-rs/core/src/client.rs: Added auth preflight in stream().
- codex-rs/core/src/codex.rs: Marked NotAuthenticated as non‑retryable in run_turn.
items.title: fix #2897: add authentication check before network requests to prevent unnecessary retries

## Summary
Fixes a bug in `wrap_ranges` where text ending with spaces could create invalid ranges that go beyond the string length.

## The Problem
When text has trailing spaces, the function calculated `end + trailing_spaces + 1` which could exceed the actual text length. This would cause a crash when trying to slice the string with that range.

## The Fix
Added a simple bounds check: `(end + trailing_spaces + 1).min(text.len())` to keep ranges valid.

## Tests
Added tests for edge cases like text with trailing spaces, empty strings, and boundary conditions.
items.title: fix: prevent out-of-bounds access in wrap_ranges function

## Summary
Fixes mutex error handling in auth functions that could crash the application.

## The Problem
Three auth functions used `.unwrap()` on mutex locks, which crashes the program if the mutex is poisoned (happens when a thread panics while holding the mutex):

```rust
self.auth_dot_json.lock().unwrap() // CRASH if mutex poisoned
```

Since these handle authentication tokens, crashes could happen during normal auth operations.

## The Fix
- Functions returning `Result` now return errors instead of crashing
- Functions returning `Option` return `None` and log errors gracefully
- Added bounds checking to prevent inconsistent auth state

## Tests
Added test to verify normal mutex behavior still works correctly.
items.title: fix: improve auth mutex error handling to prevent crashes

#### **Description**

This PR fixes an issue introduced in commit `c09ed74a` where function calls, such as `ls -la`, were being executed in the wrong directory (`~`) instead of the intended **current working directory**. This caused the Codex CLI to fail, as the content returned from function calls was incorrect.

#### **Changes Made**

- Updated the `unified_exec` function to correctly pass the **working directory** context during function calls.
- Ensured that shell commands and other functions execute in the correct directory, addressing issues like those seen with the `ls -la` command.

#### **Related Issue**

This fix addresses the issue described in [#3459](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/3459), where the working directory for function calls was incorrect.

#### **Steps to Reproduce (Before the Fix)**

1. Merge commit `c09ed74a` into the codebase.
2. Start a task and invoke a function call (e.g., `ls -la`).
3. Observe the output in the **JSONL log** where the function call is executed in the `~` directory, not the intended working directory.

#### **Expected Behavior (After the Fix)**

The function call (e.g., `ls -la`) will now execute in the correct working directory, ensuring that the content returned is accurate and the overall functionality of Codex CLI is restored.

#### **Testing**

- I have tested this fix by running a task that invokes the `ls -la` command. It now executes in the correct directory as expected.
- The Codex CLI now works as intended, and the output matches the correct file listings in the specified working directory.

#### **Additional Information**

This fix should address the issue and restore correct functionality for the Codex CLI's handling of function calls that require a specific working directory.
items.title: Fix: Ensure correct working directory for function calls in unified_exec

**What**

- Change: Update find_codex_home to resolve CODEX_HOME in this order:
      1. Project-local .codex/ in the current working directory, if present
      2. CODEX_HOME environment variable, if set
      3. Default ~/.codex
  - Behavior: When a project contains .codex/, Codex reads/writes config.toml/config.json, auth.json, logs, history, etc. from that folder, effectively overriding the global ~/.codex/ without needing flags.
  - Docs: Updated to reflect the new precedence:
      - codex-rs/README.md: Added “Project-local overrides” note
      - docs/config.md: Clarified CODEX_HOME resolution order
      - docs/authentication.md: Clarified where auth.json is read/written

  Motivation

  - Per-project isolation: Teams often need project-scoped settings (model, provider, auth) that shouldn’t bleed into other work. Resolving CODEX_HOME to a project’s .codex/ creates a clean, self-contained environment for each repo.
  - Developer experience: Switching between projects no longer requires exporting CODEX_HOME or passing flags. Just cd into the project and run codex — it automatically picks up the right config/auth.
  - Cost and policy awareness: Different projects may target different models, budgets, or retention policies. With project-local .codex/, cost controls, history settings, and provider choices live alongside the codebase, making spend, privacy, and
  compliance easier to reason about per project.
  - On-prem and special environments: Some projects must run on-prem or behind strict network policies. A project’s .codex/ can pin a specific provider/baseURL and auth configuration so teammates don’t reconfigure global settings or remember one-off
  flags.
  - Collaboration ready: Committing a template .codex/ (without secrets) documents expected defaults for contributors. Each developer adds their own auth.json locally, and everyone gets consistent behavior out of the box.
  - Backwards compatible: If .codex/ is absent, behavior is unchanged and global ~/.codex/ (or CODEX_HOME) continues to work as before.

# WHAT

  - Treat .md symlinks in $CODEX_HOME/prompts as valid custom prompts when their targets are regular files.

# WHY
  - Symlink-based dotfiles workflows are common; ignoring symlinks forces duplication and drift between canonical repos and $CODEX_HOME/prompts.

# HOW

  - Minimal change in file discovery:
      - File: codex-rs/core/src/custom_prompts.rs:35
      - Logic: accept entries that are regular files OR symlinks whose metadata resolves to a regular file:
          - ft.is_file() || (ft.is_symlink() && fs::metadata(&path).await.ok().map(|m| m.is_file()).unwrap_or(false))
      - All other behavior remains unchanged: .md filter uses symlink filename; name parsing, content loading, and front matter handling are unchanged.
  - Tests:
      - Adds a Unix-only test to assert symlinked .md discovery (target is a .txt so only the symlink shows up):
          - codex-rs/core/src/custom_prompts.rs:210
      - cargo test -p codex-core passes with no regressions.
  - Platform notes:
      - Runtime behavior is the same on Unix and Windows.
      - Windows symlink creation may require privileges, so the new test is guarded with #[cfg(unix)].
  - Security note:
      - This is intentionally the smallest possible change and will follow symlinks even if they point outside $CODEX_HOME/prompts. Symlinks may resolve outside $CODEX_HOME, but reads honor the invoking user’s OS permissions and occur pre‑model; no additional access is granted.

  This close #4383
items.title: fix: follow symlinks to files in $CODEX_HOME/prompts

I’ve been hitting the wall described in #3712: once an MCP client calls codex-reply, the server needs a stable conversationId to locate the rollout JSONL, but today that only works if the client hand-passes an absolute path. 

This PR means the MCP server can now accept either the existing rollout path or the conversation UUID that was emitted in the earlier SessionConfigured event. Under the hood that’s powered by a new `find_rollout_by_conversation_id` helper in codex-core, so both paths share the same lookup logic.

What's inside:

- Core exposes `find_rollout_by_conversation_id` so we can map a UUID back to ~/.codex/sessions/.../rollout-*.jsonl.
- `ResumeConversationParams` now takes path or `conversation_id` (both optional, at least one required) to stay compatible with existing clients.
- `resumeConversation` in the MCP server resolves the rollout path automatically when only the UUID is supplied, and returns clear JSON-RPC errors when
  neither argument is present or the UUID can’t be found.
- The resume integration test exercises both flows: resume by explicit path and resume by conversation ID only.

This should close #3712 and replaces #4374. 

I have read the CLA Document and I hereby sign the CLA

This PR updates Codex's default state directory to follow platform conventions while preserving backward compatibility.

Summary
- Precedence:
  1) If `CODEX_HOME` is set and non‑empty, use it (canonicalized).
  2) Else, if legacy `~/.codex` exists, continue using it.
  3) Else, default to `dirs::config_dir()/codex` (XDG on Linux; `~/Library/Application Support/codex` on macOS; `%AppData%\codex` on Windows).
- No change to the rest of the code: everything uses `config.codex_home` as before.

Why

items.body:
This PR addresses #4722.

## Summary

Pressing **Esc** to navigate back through previous messages would stop at the first `/status` output. Messages sent before `/status` became unreachable. This happened because `/status` output is represented as a `CompositeHistoryCell`, and the backtrack logic treated *all* composites as headers.

This PR introduces a clear distinction between **header composites** (true session starts) and **general composites** (like `/status`), then updates navigation to skip only real headers.


## Root Cause

The backtrack function skipped everything before the last composite in the transcript, assuming all composites were headers. Because `/status` also created a composite, it was mistakenly treated as a boundary, preventing access to earlier user messages.

## Fix Overview

* Added a `CompositeHistoryCellKind` enum (`Header` vs `General`) stored inside `CompositeHistoryCell`.
* Introduced `new_header()` and `is_header()` helpers to mark and identify true headers.
* Updated all session header creation sites to use `new_header(...)`.
* Rewrote backtrack logic to skip only composites marked as headers while ignoring general ones like `/status`.

## Files Changed

### **`tui/src/history_cell.rs`**

* Added the `CompositeHistoryCellKind` flag and helper methods.
* Updated session header builders to tag them as `Header`.

### **`tui/src/app_backtrack.rs`**

* Replaced the old “last composite” logic with header-aware iteration.
* Added regression tests verifying correct navigation behavior.

## Tests

* **`user_positions_skip_only_leading_composites`** – ensures `/status` no longer hides earlier user messages.
* **`user_positions_reset_after_empty_composite_boundary`** – ensures true session headers still reset navigation.

All existing tests pass successfully.

## Behavior Change

**Before:** backtracking stopped at `/status`, hiding older messages.
**After:** backtracking continues past `/status`, stopping only at real session headers.
items.title: fix(tui): allow backtracking past `/status` composites to reach earlier messages

items.body:
# fix: prevent transport idle disconnects via keepalive + heartbeats

**Why (bug):** Codex CLI sessions and workers can terminate early with
`stream error: stream disconnected before completion` after ~90–150s of idle,
breaking long-running streams and MCP transports. This PR fixes that class
of failures by keeping connections alive and aligning idle budgets across layers.

**Fixes / references:**
- **Resolves #3267** (150s cutoff; “stream closed before response.completed”).
- **Addresses #3478** (request for longer / configurable timeouts; 150s cutoff).
- **Related:** #1581 (stream closed before completion), #3835 (transport decode error), #5130 (recent disconnects).

> If maintainers prefer, I'm happy to split the “Related” references into
> follow‑ups; the core intent here is to fix the idle-disconnect bug that causes
> premature timeouts.

---

## Summary of changes
- Introduce shared HTTP client tuning (connection pool idle timeout, TCP keepalive, HTTP/2 keepalive) used by core, backends, and RMCP clients via a reusable builder helper.
- Add configurable heartbeat scheduling for MCP stdio, MCP HTTP/RMCP, and SSE streaming transports. Emit `ResponseEvent::Heartbeat` and OTEL telemetry.
- Align timeout policy so stream idle budgets exceed transport keepalive windows; clamp provider metadata + config/env overrides; warn when inconsistent.
- Extend telemetry with keepalive/idle metrics (`codex.transport.heartbeat[_sent]`, `codex.transport.idle_timeout`, `codex.transport.reconnect`) and document consumption guidance.
- Ship strace‑friendly worker harness updates (`CODEX_STRACE_CMD`) plus soak automation to validate long‑lived worker stability. Instrumentation is **off by default** and gated behind env vars.

## Configuration (new)
- `mcp.keepalive_interval_sec`
- `responses.stream_heartbeat_interval_ms`
- `transport.http.{pool_idle_timeout_secs,tcp_keepalive_secs,h2_keepalive_secs}`

**Environment overrides**
- `CODEX_MCP_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_SEC`
- `CODEX_STREAM_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS`
- `CODEX_HTTP_POOL_IDLE_S`, `CODEX_TCP_KEEPALIVE_S`, `CODEX_H2_KEEPALIVE_S`

**Defaults** target ≥5‑minute idle budgets (pool idle 330s, TCP keepalive 30s, SSE heartbeat 45s).
Setting a heartbeat interval to `0` disables the loop.

## Backwards-compatibility & risk
- **Behavioral change:** improved liveness only; no user‑visible API changes.
- **Safe defaults:** off‑by‑default instrumentation; timeouts remain configurable.
- **Opt‑out:** set heartbeat interval to `0` to disable.
- **No breaking changes** to Node entrypoint behavior; strace launcher is strictly feature‑gated via `CODEX_STRACE_CMD`.

## Validation
- `cargo +stable fmt`
- `PATH="$PWD/target/debug:$PATH" cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-targets`
- `PATH="$PWD/target/debug:$PATH" cargo +stable test --workspace`
- **Soak runs** (stdio/rmcp 300s; SSE 900s) via `scripts/codex/analysis/run_idle_soak_suite.sh` with strace instrumentation:
  - `20251011-smoke-soak-mined-summary.json`: max idle wait 0.200s; no disconnects.
  - `20251011-222535-soak-mined-summary.json`: max waits 217s / 262s / 270s under 900s threshold.
  - `20251012` suite: stdio & RMCP **PASS** @300s; SSE aborted at ~455s with **early DONE** (distinct from idle timeout; see notes).
- Long soak (3600s stdio/rmcp, 14400s SSE) artifacts available on request (excluded for size).

**Notes on SSE early-DONE:** observed once at ~455s; strace shows long `futex` waits, no socket close. This appears orthogonal to transport idle. Happy to re‑run with a stricter harness, but it doesn’t invalidate this idle‑disconnect fix.

## Docs
- `codex/codex-rs/docs/config.md`
- `docs/codex/analysis/keepalive-telemetry.md`
- `docs/codex/analysis/soak_idle_keepalive.md`

---

### Checklist
- [x] Rebased on `openai/codex:main` (feature/transport-keepalive).
- [x] Updated configuration + telemetry docs.
- [x] Captured validation evidence in repo (`docs/codex/analysis/pr-bundle/`).
- [ ] Obtain maintainer review.

## What

This PR fixes the Homebrew update flow by ensuring `brew update` is run before `brew upgrade --cask codex`.

## Why

When Codex is installed via Homebrew, the internal updater was running `brew upgrade --cask codex` directly without first syncing the cask index via `brew update`. This caused Homebrew to use a stale cask index and incorrectly report "already latest" even when a newer version existed upstream.

## How

Modified `run_update_action` in `codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs` to detect when `UpdateAction::BrewUpgrade` is being executed and run `brew update` first before the upgrade command.

The fix:
1. Checks if the update action is `BrewUpgrade`
2. If so, runs `brew update` to sync the cask index
3. Then proceeds with the normal `brew upgrade --cask codex` command

Fixes #6253, #5607, #5515

---

**Note:** I've read and agree to the CLA. This is my first contribution to Codex!

This fixes an issue where pressing Enter on the second visual line of the chat composer (after the input wraps) no longer submits on some Windows consoles. The underlying problem is that certain terminals don’t reliably report Shift for Enter or don’t support keyboard enhancement flags, which makes the code think the key is not a plain Enter and thus inserts a newline instead of submitting.

What’s changed
- Introduce `is_plain_enter()` to normalize Enter handling in `ChatComposer`.
- When keyboard enhancement flags are supported, behavior is unchanged: Enter submits; Shift+Enter inserts a newline.
- When not supported (notably some Windows consoles), treat Enter as submit as long as Ctrl/Alt aren’t held. This makes Enter work consistently even after the input wraps to multiple visual lines.

Why
- Repro on Windows: type a first line, press Enter submits; type a long line to wrap and press Enter—on some consoles, Enter is reported with an unexpected modifier and doesn’t submit.

Testing
- Verified logic paths for both enhanced and non‑enhanced terminals.
- No change to typical Unix terminals or modern Windows terminals that support enhancements (Shift+Enter still inserts newline there).

Notes
- This PR is conservative: it only broadens the definition of “plain Enter” in environments without keyboard enhancement support. It should be safe for production and improves UX on affected Windows setups.

Fixes #6307
items.title: TUI: make Enter submit reliably on Windows when input wraps (fallback when keyboard enhancements unsupported)

v0.14.0

This release marks an important milestone for tonic, "hopefully" this will be the last major breaking release of Tonic before we start to transition work into bringing the community a joint-effort grpc-rust implementation. For the moment, any new features for the core of tonic that are not related to the work towards grpc-rust will not be accepted (I believe tonic to be in quite a good spot, security features of course will be handled with the upmost importance). Stay tuned there will be more information the coming months on what is going on with the new project but you can already see some of the code in the grpc crate within the tonic repository.

You can always watch this video for more info on grpc-rust.

Breaking Changes

  • Prost updated to v0.14
  • Prost has been extracted to their own crates

Migration guide

To migrate between <=v0.13.1 to v0.14 anything that used prost has now been moved into either tonic-prost or tonic-prost-build. All the previous types are still available but under these two new crates.

items.body:
Fixes #6450 - unified exec broken on linux since 0.57.0

The Linux sandbox binary was failing to parse command-line arguments due to missing clap attributes on the `command` field. This caused the error "unexpected argument '--sandbox-policy-cwd' found" when unified_exec was enabled on Linux.

Added `allow_hyphen_values = true` to allow command arguments that start with hyphens (e.g., `ls -la`) to be properly parsed as part of the trailing command instead of being interpreted as options to the sandbox binary itself.

Added `num_args = 1..` to make the argument requirements more explicit for clap's parser.

These attributes ensure the argument parser correctly handles:
- The --sandbox-policy-cwd and --sandbox-policy named arguments
- The -- separator
- The trailing command arguments (which may contain flags)

Docs link: https://docs.rs/clap/latest/clap/builder/struct.Arg.html#method.trailing_var_arg
items.title: fix: Add clap attributes for proper argument parsing in linux-sandbox
